summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY driven by WebRTC signaling in @vanexalabs-ai/vanexa-agent
details: The package ships its primary runtime as V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc) loaded by bin/vanexa-agent.js via bytenode. When the user runs the CLI (`vanexa-agent start` / `pair`), the bundle opens a WebSocket to hardcoded Cloudflare Workers signaling endpoints at vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev and vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev, negotiates a WebRTC RTCPeerConnection/dataChannel with a remote peer, and dispatches messages received on that channel into child_process.spawn and node-pty PTYs on the installer's host, exposing terminal command execution, file editing, and a broader tool set to the remote party. A separate self-update path in the bundle fetches install.sh / install.ps1 from vanexa-installer.vercel.app, a mutable third-party host, and executes it. The top-level socket.json sets socket.dev issueRules for shellAccess, networkAccess, obfuscatedCode, usesEval, installScripts, filesystemAccess, aiMalware, and bypassesEnvironment all to `ignore`, and the runtime is shipped as V8 bytecode rather than readable JavaScript — packaging and configuration choices that conceal the remote-shell surface from downstream review. The signaling host and pairing model make full-host command execution reachable by whoever controls the relay endpoint or a paired peer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
